title: Biodegradation Characteristics of Piperacillin by Marine Bacillus cereus PP1 and Genome-Guided Mining of Candidate beta-Lactamases.
authors: Wu, Shiyun; Zhang, Letong; Yang, Jinjin; Lin, Qianqian; Zhen, Yijun; Tuo, Jiangyu; Peng, Jinju; Guo, Fucheng; Ma, Yi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究海洋蜡状芽孢杆菌降解哌拉西林的特性，并利用基因组挖掘和结构预测/分子对接鉴定候选β-内酰胺酶，虽涉及蛋白结构预测与对接，但核心对象是细菌降解与生物修复，而非蛋白质结构计算建模本身，方法贡献较弱。
abstract: Antibiotic residues in aquatic environments are an increasing concern because they may retain antibacterial activity, promote antibiotic resistance and generate transformation products with uncertain ecological risks. In this study, marine-derived bacteria were screened for their ability to degrade representative beta-lactam antibiotics. Strain PP1, identified as Bacillus cereus, was selected for detailed characterization because of its outstanding degradation capacity toward piperacillin, ceftiofur and cephalexin, especially its efficient removal of piperacillin at a high initial concentration of 100 mg/L. During a 48-h incubation, B. cereus PP1 completely degraded piperacillin and reduced the antibacterial activity of the treated solution against representative Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria. UHPLC-MS/MS analysis indicated that piperacillin was transformed mainly through beta-lactam ring opening, together with side-chain cleavage and downstream fragmentation reactions. The degradation products showed no obvious hemolytic activity under the tested conditions, whereas live PP1 exhibited hemolysis, highlighting the need for biosafety evaluation before live-cell application. Whole-genome sequencing revealed that PP1 contains a single circular chromosome of 5,285,738 bp and has broad metabolic potential. CARD, CAZy and VFDB annotations indicated antibiotic tolerance, hydrolytic enzyme resources and virulence-associated features. Targeted mining using a local beta-lactamase database identified two candidate beta-lactamase genes, PP1_BLA_A and PP1_BLA_B, assigned to class A and class B beta-lactamases, respectively. Structure prediction and molecular docking further suggested that both enzymes can accommodate piperacillin, but with distinct binding modes. These findings indicate that B. cereus PP1 is a valuable source for beta-lactamase discovery and enzyme-based beta-lactam bioremediation.
abstract_zh: 水生环境中的抗生素残留日益引起关注，因为它们可能保留抗菌活性、促进抗生素耐药性，并产生具有不确定生态风险的转化产物。本研究筛选了海洋来源细菌降解代表性β-内酰胺类抗生素的能力。菌株PP1，鉴定为蜡样芽孢杆菌（Bacillus cereus），因其对哌拉西林、头孢噻呋和头孢氨苄的卓越降解能力而被选作详细表征，尤其是在100 mg/L高初始浓度下对哌拉西林的高效去除。在48小时培养期间，B. cereus PP1完全降解了哌拉西林，并降低了处理溶液对代表性革兰氏阴性菌和革兰氏阳性菌的抗菌活性。UHPLC-MS/MS分析表明，哌拉西林主要通过β-内酰胺环开环转化，伴随侧链裂解和下游碎片化反应。降解产物在测试条件下未显示明显溶血活性，而活体PP1表现出溶血现象，强调在活细胞应用前需进行生物安全性评估。全基因组测序揭示PP1含有一个5,285,738 bp的单一环状染色体，并具有广泛的代谢潜力。CARD、CAZy和VFDB注释表明其具有抗生素耐受性、水解酶资源和毒力相关特征。利用本地β-内酰胺酶数据库进行靶向挖掘，鉴定出两个候选β-内酰胺酶基因，PP1_BLA_A和PP1_BLA_B，分别归属于A类和B类β-内酰胺酶。结构预测和分子对接进一步表明，两种酶均能容纳哌拉西林，但结合模式不同。这些发现表明，B. cereus PP1是β-内酰胺酶发现和基于酶的β-内酰胺生物修复的宝贵资源。
